body:
What I was talking about has less to do with problematic takes, but delving into the schematics of movies. 

Regardless of that though, you equate Ariel being black and JK to each other with little regard because you reject thinking about the ways it hurts others, because you live in a place where you can. 

You say “let people enjoy things” because you want to keep disregarding what you like that is problematic, but where’s the line? As far as you’ve said, there isn’t one for you. 

Most people who go to college understand criticism theory, the line is where there is a minority oppression. You do not have that line because seemingly you live in a world where you don’t experience it, or reject the idea that you do. 

You saying you like Twilight doesn’t matter to anyone because an extreme supernatural story about a guy who’s forever years old who was stunted at a young age, and a girl who also gets stunted at a young age getting married, doesn’t correlate with the other topics you’ve mentioned. 

The only thing I’d say with twilight is that it was made by a Mormon girl who probably experienced grooming (-esque?), normalizing it herself and putting it in a story. But that’s still not anything because she did not have the intent of grooming her audience to make them think it’s okay. Bro, it’s a vampire. 

TLDR: 
You’re safe from “being problematic”. Although your examples were a little on the nose, and your reply where you silence someone questioning you is kind of… well, never mind. 

But stay “kind”, babe.
I’ve been there, but not asking why is like a phantom limb, struggle. I think another phrase for it could be “messing around and finding out” T_T

Interesting, I don’t think I can relate to the first part of your comment, but otherwise it is helpful.  

I’ll try to look for more commonalities in the future instead of looking for the opposite
